data.name: The Puppet of Tersa: Episode One
data.detailed_description:
ABOUT THIS GAME:
This episodic storybook tale takes place in an era of the past, before computers and smartphones, when children solved problems through exploration and creativity. It is a point-and-click narrative adventure presented in a hand-drawn style that blends childlike innocence with something darker.

The Puppet of Tersa is a five episode series. Through each episode, Cynthia delves deeper into the world of Tersa, a place both whimsical and creepy, with bizarre creatures and unusual inhabitants. In her search for a way home. Searching for answers, making new friends, and solving puzzles and problems that will ultimately allow her to confront the mysterious force that keeps Cynthia from going home. Cynthia’s story begins with the first episode, The Puppet of Tersa: A Curious Place.


KEY FEATURES:

  • Advancement Through Puzzles:
    The core foundation of gameplay requires Cynthia to solve puzzles in order to progress.

  • Experiment with Interactions:
    Nearly everything in the game is interactive, providing players with tools needed to solve puzzles and the opportunity to learn more about the world of Tersa.

  • Digitally Hand-Painted, 2D Style:
    The world of Tersa is digitally hand-painted using specialized brushes to give the presence of the artist's hand at work.

reviews.review:
The Puppet of Tersa is a charming episodic adventure game set in a fantasy world. The games hand-drawn graphics and bizarre characters grant a unique and enjoyable experience for all adventure and puzzle game enthusiasts. 

[u] Pros[/u]
+ Beautiful hand-drawn graphics and aesthetics.
+ Immersive and whimsical story-telling told through the innocent eyes of a child whilst incorporating darker themes.
+ Lots of objects to interact with.
+ Abundance of character dialogue.
+ Active developers responding to community feedback 

[u] Cons[/u]
- No voice overs for any dialogue
-[i] Nitpick[/i] Short game length of approximately 2 hours for the first episode.
- [i] Nitpick[/i] Lack of difficulty in puzzle progression.

[h1] Story[/h1]
Episode one begins and you are introduced to the protagonist, an ordinary and innocent young girl named Cynthia. Shortly after this brief introduction, you find yourself transported far from reality and into the depths of an unknown, peculiar world. This extravagant new world is littered with strange looking beings that look like they belong in old children's fairy tales. Early on, you become acquainted with the most adorable fairy-like creature who will remain by your side for the remainder of the episode and aid you in completing tasks. The main goal is to escape this intriguing yet frightening world and return to the safety of your home ... however, this is not as easy as it seems.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The point and click gameplay consists of what many adventure addicts are accustomed to, puzzles! The puzzles featured are not challenging nor overly easy however I would like to see more progression in the difficulty as the episodes continue. The puzzles are varied and range from putting items in the correct order to untangling cords and so forth. 

The other majority of the time, if not completing puzzles, will be spent speaking to the various characters scattered throughout the map. Conversing with the characters will enable progression through the game and also lead the player in the right direction on how to complete a specific task. The game has complete and easy to read English subtitles with no faulty grammar


[h1]Characters[/h1]
Each character is unique and has their own mannerisms. It is evident that ample time was spent on crafting these personas and the way they speak which makes conversing with them quite enjoyable. It seems to me like a lot of inspiration was taken from children's movies or fairy tales and this has been mixed in with some darker overtones. This combination creates an array of interesting dialogue and I look forward to future characters in the upcoming episodes. 

[h1] Graphics[/h1]
The most eye-catching aspect of this game is by far the beautiful graphics and attention to detail. The artistic digitally painted design is immaculate and engrosses the player into a child-like atmosphere, just with a darker twist. 

[h1]Sound[/h1]
Although there is no audio voice overs for any of the dialogue, the soundtrack does wonders for the game and further compliments the story-telling. It is also available for purchase as DLC.

[h1]Bugs and glitches[/h1]
I did not encounter any glitches and had seamless gameplay. Upon reading through posts in the discussion page, it seems the developer is working hard to patch any bugs that arise which is fantastic. 

[h1] Price and content[/h1]
This first episode is adequately priced at $9.95 for approximately two hours of gameplay. The story will be spread over 5 episodes with each episode looking to be sold separately, however the developers are still considering their options. 

[h1] Conclusion[/h1]
Being Madorium's first published point and click game is commendable and the effort that has gone into the Tersa series is considerable. I look forward to see where this bizarre world will take Cynthia and am eager to explore more of this imaginative realm in future episodes.

[i] This product was reviewed using a free key provided by the developers.[/i]
